1181-program-description-2: Chemistry of Earth's lithosphere, its reactions with air and water, and of extra-terrestrial materials. Needs CHEM 110 and 120, and MATH 139 and 141, or equivalents.
1181-program-description-3: Core geology, geophysics, Earth systems and planetary science, with flexible courses from other sciences or arts for an interdisciplinary degree.
1182-complementary-courses-24-credits: 3 from a pair and 21 from the list. Science and Engineering courses at 300+ may count with the Director's permission.
1182-program-description: Rigorous foundations and advanced topics for energy, mineral and ore exploration and environmental geoscience. Meets academic requirements of Canadian professional orders for geologists.
1183-complementary-courses-36-credits: 15 of advanced earth science, 3 of environmental and ore-forming processes, and 18 of other specializations. Other ATOC, EPSC, ESYS, GEOG, MATH and MIME courses may count with permission if they meet professional order requirements.
1184-complementary-courses-33-credits: 15 of earth science, 3 of environmental and ore-forming processes, and 15 of other specializations. Other departments' courses may count with permission if they meet professional order requirements.
1184-program-description: Rigorous physical science with an individualized plan for industry, teaching, research or graduate work. Keep CGPA 3.20.
1185-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from a pair and 9 from the list. Science and Engineering courses at 300+ may count with the Director's permission.
1186-about-earth-system-science: Six Grand Challenges: biogeochemical cycles; climate; land use; energy and resources; hazards like volcanoes, earthquakes and hurricanes; and Earth-atmosphere observation and prediction.

Many go on to M.Sc. or Ph.D. study. Others work in environmental consulting, disaster risk at re-insurers, product life cycle management, and software for farming or inventory. Offered jointly by ATOC (p. 1126), EPSC (p. 1180) and GEOG (p. 1197).
1186-program-advisor: Dr. William Minarik, Frank Dawson Adams, Room 215, 3450 Rue University.
1186-program-description: Quantitative tools for connections among atmosphere, oceans, solid Earth, and ecological and human processes, relevant to sustainability and climate, across deep time and the Anthropocene.
1186-complementary-courses-6-credits: 3 credits each from two of EPSC, ATOC or GEOG, at 300+, with the adviser.
1186-program-description-2: Earth as one system, jointly by ATOC, EPSC and GEOG: how matter and energy cycle through the atmosphere, biosphere, cryosphere, exosphere and hydrosphere, and how biological, chemical, human and physical parts link over days to billions of years.
1187-complementary-courses-39-credits: 3 credits from each of eight small lists, then 15 from the long list, with 3+ each of ATOC, EPSC and GEOG, and 9+ at 400+. Science and Engineering courses at 300+ may count with permission. MATH 315 is required for Honours.
1188-program-description: Joint by ATOC, EPSC and GEOG: a rigorous, individualized program for industry, teaching, research or graduate work. CGPA 3.20 to register and graduate. First Class: CGPA 3.70, program GPA 3.20, and B+ in ESYS 300, 301 and 500.
1189-complementary-courses-39-credits: 3 credits from each of eight small lists, then 15 from the long list, with 3+ each of ATOC, EPSC and GEOG, and 9+ at 400+. Science and Engineering courses at 300+ may count with permission.
1191-about-entrepreneurship-for-science-: Six courses adding business skills to technical knowledge, for high-tech start-ups and small or medium firms.
1191-program-description: With Desautels: an entrepreneurial mindset and method, across ventures, social enterprise, tech start-ups, co-ops, corporate ventures and side projects. Self-directed and hands-on, with group projects at live McGill start-ups.
1192-environment: See the Bieler School of Environment, including the Major.
1193-about-clinical-and-translational-re: Formerly Experimental Medicine, a division of Medicine. No B.Sc. programs, but EXMD courses count as Science.
1193-location: Department of Medicine, 1001 Decarie Blvd., H4A 3J1.
1196-about-the-general-science-minor: Only for B.Sc. Liberal students; see the Advisor.
1196-program-description: For Liberal students as their breadth component. See your core program adviser and the Interdisciplinary Programs Adviser.
1196-complementary-courses-18-credits: Science courses at 200+, different from your core. Either 9 at 300+ and 9+ outside your core subject, or 12 at 300+ and 6+ outside. 396 and 397 research courses don't count.
1197-programs-offered: B.A., B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc. See pp. 516 and 233.
1197-location: Burnside Hall, floors 3–7, 805 Sherbrooke St. W. Office: Room 305. Undergraduate Advisor: Michelle Maillet, Room 322.
1198-program-description-3: Holistic environmental science including human and climatic elements. Required courses prepare you for 300-level work; complementaries add analysis and physical geography for 400–500 level study.
1199-complementary-courses-36-credits: 3 of statistics (see Course Overlap), 9 of systematic physical geography, 9 across environmental analysis and Environment, Earth System and Sustainability Sciences (6 and 3 either way), 9 on human-environment links, 3 of field courses, and 3 of approved advanced courses.
1200-program-description: Theory and tools of physical geography: how physical, chemical and biological processes shape environments and ecosystem services, and sustainability for communities. Core in geomorphology, hydrology, soil biogeochemistry, biogeography and climatology, with field courses, quantitative methods, GIS and remote sensing.
1200-complementary-courses-45-credits: 3 of statistics (see Course Overlap), 9 of systematic physical geography, 3 of field courses (availability set each February), 15 across environmental analysis and Environment, Earth System and Sustainability Sciences (9 and 6 either way), 9 on human-environment links, and 6 of approved advanced courses. 500-level needs the instructor's permission; don't take more than one a term.
